annotations.annotation_text: The half-title of James Joyce's final masterwork. For seventeen years (1922–1939), Joyce kept the title a strictly guarded secret, referring to the manuscript exclusively as 'Work in Progress'. Only Joyce and his wife Nora Barnacle knew the title until its formal announcement at a Paris publication dinner on Joyce's fifty-seventh birthday (February 2, 1939).
sources: Ellmann, Richard. James Joyce. Oxford University Press, 1982.
Slocum, John J., and Herbert Cahoon. A Bibliography of James Joyce. Yale University Press, 1953.

annotations.annotation_text: Joyce composed the text in Paris under conditions of near-blindness and failing health, assisted by Samuel Beckett, Stuart Gilbert, Frank Budgen, Eugene Jolas, and Paul Léon. The work synthesizes over sixty languages into a polyphonic dream-fugue.
sources: Ellmann, Richard. James Joyce. Oxford University Press, 1982.
Budgen, Frank. James Joyce and the Making of Ulysses and Other Writings. Oxford University Press, 1972.
